findings.title: Policy errors are downgraded to durable grants in compound transport
findings.issue: execute_reserved_groups catches Exception around grant re-validation and transport, then settles each prepared operation as 'unknown' and re-raises; but the initial loop calling _commit_durable_transport falls inside the same try and any StorageError/KeyError from those calls is also funneled through that path, while _commit_durable_transport itself returns False on all storage faults and the caller converts that to CapabilityDenied. A DB outage during pre-transport authorization therefore yields a retryable-looking CapabilityDenied for operations that were actually already prepared in prior (
findings.fix: Return a fail-closed outcome distinguishing 'denied before any prepared operation' from 'authorization state unavailable after preparation', and never mark partially prepared groups as retryable. Treat storage faults after the first successful _commit_durable_transport as unknown outcomes requiring reconciliation, not CapabilityDenied.

findings.title: Unknown model outcomes can be silently retried by callers
findings.issue: complete_with_receipt converts every transport exception (including a response that exceeded the 1MB bound or had a malformed body) into LLMOutcomeUnknown with external_call_attempted=True and raises it, but the caller-visible exception does not itself carry a fence that prevents a subsequent retry from issuing a second real network call for the same reservation. The durable operation is settled 'unknown' (not replayable) via execute_reserved_groups' except path, yet ScopedModelClient gives no guarantee the higher-level retry loop won't construct a fresh request/reservation pair and call again
findings.fix: Make the unknown receipt reference a durable idempotency/operation fence that any retry path must check before re-issuing I/O, and document/enforce that LLMOutcomeUnknown never re-invokes transport. Add a test asserting a second attempt after unknown is blocked.

findings.title: apply_domain_delta can erase target-only tombstones' side effects inconsistently
findings.issue: After replacing all domain tables with source rows, apply_domain_delta re-runs delete_derived_in for each tombstone row. delete_derived_in rebuilds/updates dependent records (conversation history, delivery attempts, cache entries, jobs) based only on current content; for tombstones that existed on the target but whose derived artifacts were already cleaned up locally, re-running deletion on a freshly imported state can re-write '[deleted by owner]' payloads or re-cancel jobs that the target had already finalized, producing non-monotone side effects despite the stated monotone guarantee.
findings.fix: Make delete_derived_in's secondary updates strictly monotone/idempotent (e.g., only touch rows whose current payload still contains the original private text, or record an explicit deletion-applied marker), and add a regression test applying the same tombstone twice across import boundaries.

not_verified: Whether call sites of LLMOutcomeUnknown enforce retry blocking
Whether schema/foreign-key order assumptions in apply_domain_delta hold for all listed tables
Actual test coverage for the compound-group failure paths in execute_reserved_groups
findings.summary: Reviewed the phase F diff for fail-closed policy, migration monotonicity, and unknown-outcome handling. The code is generally careful about fencing, bounded payloads, and egress gating, but compound scope-group transport conflates pre-authorization storage failures with CapabilityDenied (retryable), model unknown outcomes lack an enforced no-retry fence at the client boundary, and tombstone re-application across domain import may produce non-monotone side effects. No P0 issues were identified in the supplied diff; address the listed P1 items before treating this as release-ready.
